title: CLO 2026.0 - 3D
description: CLO 2026.0 version is now officially released — Make it, for real! CLO technical experts provide a detailed explanation of the 3D updates: importing design curves drawn in vector-level smooth modeling software via OBJ, maintaining 3D model state when scaling 2D panels, isolated selection, GPU attachments...
transcript:
In version 2026.0, you can now directly view the mass frequency curve NURBS in CLO and convert them into 3D pen lines.  
This video will guide you through the entire workflow, from creating a curve in mass frequency modeling software to editing and generating panels in CLO.  
Let's see how it works.  

First, create a curve for the object in the NURBS software.  
After creating the curve, export the object and import it into CLO.  
Open the virtual model information display and show the NURBS curve to view the curve.  
You can see that the curve is imported with the object.  
Right-click on the curve and select the 3D pen virtual model option.  
Click this option to convert the curve into a 3D pen curve.  
When the virtual model is enabled, the generated 3D pen will be displayed as a green line.  

Next, use the same method to convert the remaining curves into 3D pen lines.  
Use the 3D pen virtual model tool to shorten the curve.  
The curve points will not automatically connect, so you need to manually merge them.  
Move the curve points.  
When the distance between points is close enough, they will automatically merge.  
Merge the remaining points.  
For 3D pen curves with a larger angle, right-click and select duplicate to the edge of the grid.  
Make it fit the edge of the grid.  

Now all points have been merged.  
Let's perform the flatten operation.  
After flattening, you can see that the curve line is created.  
Furthermore, after flattening, the curves will automatically merge together.  
If necessary, you can manually adjust the merged lines.  
Using this function, you can create a flat pattern more accurately and efficiently from a mass and smooth modeling object.  

Here, we can literally consider it as a flat line.  

Product  

Let's look at how this function helps simplify the design process.  
First, use the adjustment panel tool to select the garment panels you want to store.  
Drag the storage handle to the inside or outside of the storage handle in the upper right corner, and store the selected panels proportionally.  
When you release the mouse, you can see the 2D panel changes, and the 3D window updates simultaneously.  
The 3D garment after storage still maintains its original simulation shape and proportion.  

Note that 3D position optimization will only be triggered to maintain the overall shape of the 3D model when multiple panels are stored simultaneously.  
When storing a single panel or performing non-standard proportional storage that adjusts only width or height, the original conventional processing method will still be maintained.  

For 3D models with garments, the function can intelligently process stored clothes.  
Point-like garments, such as buttons, will retain their original size and automatically move with the 3D model.  
The 3D model will be stored in the correct position after storage, and the 3D model will be stored with the same length to match the new panel size.  

If you are processing a full set of multiple layers, you can select the entire set of garments.  
Even after significant size changes, the relative position and spiral shape of each layer can be maintained without any conflict or collision.  

2026.0 Version Update  

The 3D model one-key function is equivalent to a search function.  
While adjusting the size of the 2D panel, remodeling is not required to perfectly maintain the 3D shape.  
This function automatically adapts the size and position of the garments and can completely retain the original 3D spiral effect and overall shape,  
thus helping you efficiently generate multiple size documents of the same model.  

2026.0 Version Update  

In version 2026.0, the 3D window vertical menu Azul Shepherd adds an isolation selection function.  

This function can hide all irrelevant content in the 3D window, allowing you to clearly see specific pattern materials or model components.  
This is very useful when working with complex designs that have multiple layers.  

Let's look at how to apply this tool.  
Editing multiple layers of clothing has become easier.  
For example, if you want to edit the vest under this lady’s shirt,  
you don’t need to manually hide the outer clothing layer.  
Simply select the vest pattern in the 2D or 3D window,  
then click the isolation selection icon at the bottom of the 3D vertical menu bar,  
or directly press the Shift + I shortcut keys.  

The 3D window will only display the selected content,  
allowing you to fully focus on the inner clothing layer without visual distractions.  
This way, you can quickly and intuitively adjust the inner garment,  
for example, you can check more clearly and change the print type on the vest.  

Please note that isolation display is only activated for the content selected at that moment.  
If you select other content, the isolation display content will not update automatically.  

To restore the display of all content,  
simply click the isolation selection icon again or press Shift + I.  
This tool only affects the display in the 3D window  
and does not change the final image rendering.  

The isolation selection also works for garments such as buttons.  
Select a button and activate the isolation selection tool,  
so you can adjust it freely without disturbance.  

In version 2026.0, you no longer need to manually hide or show individual items to clearly see the operation;  
use isolation selection to remove obstructions, focus on the design,  
and the most important details.  

In previous versions,  
the collision calculation for buttons and chains was fully handled by the CPU.  
As the number of buttons increased, simulation speed sometimes slowed down.  

From version 2026.0,  
buttons also support GPU simulation,  
which significantly improves overall work efficiency.  

Let’s look at this function together.  
First, long-press the simulation tool for 2 seconds  
to ensure GPU simulation is activated,  
then start the simulation.  

You can see that even with belt decorations and multiple metal items,  
the dynamic simulation of the skirt runs smoothly without lag.  
The simulation quality matches the CPU simulation, maintaining the same high level of accuracy.  

Currently, GPU simulation only supports Windows systems,  
but GPU simulation runs smoothly.  

With GPU simulation,  
you can now complete complex configuration designs more quickly.  

We hope this update assists you in your creative process.

chunks.title: CLO 2026.0 - 3D
chunks.content: # CLO 2026.0 - 3D Features and Workflow This document covers key features and workflows introduced in CLO version 2026.0, focusing on NURBS curve integration, 3D pen conversion, garment panel storage, 3D model optimization, isolation selection, and GPU simulation enhancements. It provides detailed technical procedures and functional explanations to optimize 3D garment design and simulation. --- ## NURBS Curve Integration and 3D Pen Conversion This section explains how to import NURBS curves from external software into CLO, convert them into 3D pen lines, and prepare these curves for flat pattern generation. ### Workflow for Importing and Converting NURBS Curves - Create the curve in a mass frequency NURBS modeling software. - Export the object containing the curve and import it into CLO. - Open the Virtual Model Information display and enable the NURBS curve view to verify the imported curve. - Right-click the curve and select the **3D Pen Virtual Model** option to convert it into a 3D pen curve. - The converted 3D pen curve appears as a green line in the 3D window. ### Editing and Merging 3D Pen Curves - Repeat the conversion process for all curves. - Use the 3D pen virtual model tool to shorten curves as needed. - Curve points do not automatically connect; manually move points to merge them. - When points are close enough, they automatically merge. - For curves with sharp angles, duplicate the curve to the grid edge and adjust to fit precisely. - Once all points are merged, perform a **Flatten** operation. - Flattening merges curves automatically and creates a flat pattern line. - Manual adjustment of merged lines is possible for precision. - This process enables accurate and efficient flat pattern creation from smooth mass modeling objects. --- ## Garment Panel Storage and 3D Position Optimization This section covers how to use CLO’s adjustment panel tool to store and proportionally resize garment panels while maintaining 3D simulation integrity and garment relationships. ### Using the Adjustment Panel Tool - Select garment panels to store using the adjustment panel tool. - Drag the storage handle inward or outward in the upper right corner to proportionally store selected panels. - Upon releasing the mouse, the 2D panels update proportionally, and the 3D garment shape updates simultaneously. - The 3D garment retains its original simulation shape and proportions after storage. ### Storage Behavior and Optimization - When storing multiple panels simultaneously, CLO triggers 3D position optimization to maintain the overall 3D model shape. - Storing a single panel or non-standard proportional storage (adjusting only width or height) uses conventional processing without 3D optimization. - Point-like garments (e.g., buttons) retain their original size and move automatically with the 3D model. - The 3D model adjusts to the correct position and length to match resized panels. ### Multi-Layer Garment Storage - Entire garment layers can be selected and stored together. - Even with significant size changes, relative positions and spiral shapes of each layer are preserved without conflicts or collisions.

chunks.content: - Storing a single panel or non-standard proportional storage (adjusting only width or height) uses conventional processing without 3D optimization. - Point-like garments (e.g., buttons) retain their original size and move automatically with the 3D model. - The 3D model adjusts to the correct position and length to match resized panels. ### Multi-Layer Garment Storage - Entire garment layers can be selected and stored together. - Even with significant size changes, relative positions and spiral shapes of each layer are preserved without conflicts or collisions. --- ## 3D Model One-Key Function for Size Adjustment This feature allows resizing 2D panels without remodeling, maintaining the 3D shape and spiral effects automatically. - Acts as a search and adapt function for 3D garment resizing. - Automatically adjusts garment size and position to perfectly retain the original 3D spiral effect and overall shape. - Facilitates efficient creation of multiple size documents for the same model. --- ## Isolation Selection Function in 3D Window Introduced in version 2026.0, the isolation selection tool simplifies editing complex multi-layer garments by hiding irrelevant content in the 3D window. ### Functionality and Usage - Hides all non-selected pattern materials or model components in the 3D window. - Ideal for focusing on specific inner garment layers without visual distractions. - To activate: - Select the desired garment or component in the 2D or 3D window. - Click the isolation selection icon in the 3D vertical menu or press **Shift + I**. - The 3D window displays only the selected content. - Allows clearer editing, such as changing print types on inner garments. - Isolation display remains fixed to the initially selected content and does not update automatically with other selections. - To restore full display, click the icon again or press **Shift + I**. - Only affects 3D window visibility, not final image rendering. ### Additional Notes - Works with point-like garments such as buttons, enabling isolated adjustments. - Eliminates the need to manually hide or show layers or items. --- ## GPU Simulation for Buttons and Metal Accessories In version 2026.0, button and similar accessory simulations now support GPU acceleration, improving simulation speed and efficiency. ### Previous Simulation Method - Collision calculations for buttons and chains were CPU-based. - Increasing numbers of buttons could slow simulation performance. ### GPU Simulation Improvements - Activate GPU simulation by long-pressing the simulation tool for 2 seconds. - Start the simulation; GPU acceleration handles dynamic simulations of belts, buttons, and metal decorations smoothly. - Maintains the same high accuracy as CPU simulation. - Currently supported only on Windows systems. - Enables faster completion of complex configuration designs with numerous metal components. --- # Summary CLO 2026.0 introduces significant enhancements including direct NURBS curve import and conversion to 3D pen lines for precise flat pattern creation, advanced garment panel storage with 3D shape retention, an isolation selection tool for focused editing in complex multi-layer garments, and GPU-accelerated simulation for buttons and metal accessories for improved performance.
